introduction: On this first Sunday of Lent, Genesis tells how the first man and woman, tempted by the serpent, disobeyed God. In the Gospel, Jesus, led by the Spirit into the desert, fasts forty days and overcomes the devil's temptations with the word of God. Paul tells us that where sin came through one man, grace overflows through Jesus Christ. Let us begin our Lenten journey with Jesus.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, where sin increased, grace overflowed. Let us bring our prayers to the God of mercy.
intentions: For the Church: that this Lent may be a time of conversion and renewal for all her members. Let us pray to the Lord.
For catechumens preparing for Baptism at Easter: that they may be strengthened against every temptation. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are tempted: that, like Jesus, they may find strength in the word of God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the hungry, for whom fasting is not a choice: that our Lenten sacrifices may help to feed them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that our prayer, fasting and almsgiving may draw us closer to God. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, your Son overcame temptation in the desert. Strengthen us this Lent to resist evil, to live by your word, and to worship you alone. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: In the desert
reflection.body:
The first reading takes us back to the beginning. God forms the man from the dust and breathes life into him, and places him in a garden full of good things. Then the serpent comes with a question that plants doubt: "Has God really said," that they must not eat of any tree of the garden? He suggests that God is holding something back, and promises, "you will be like God." The woman and the man eat, and "Their eyes were opened, and they both knew that they were naked." Temptation promised everything; it brought shame and fear.

In the Gospel, Jesus goes into the desert, led by the Spirit, and fasts forty days. The tempter comes to him too, with the same strategy: doubt about who he is ("If you are the Son of God"), and shortcuts. Turn stones into bread. Throw yourself from the temple and force God to rescue you. Worship the devil and receive all the kingdoms of the world.

Where Adam and Eve failed, Jesus stands firm. He answers each temptation with the word of God: "Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of God's mouth." "You shall not test the Lord, your God." And finally, "Get behind me, Satan! For it is written," and he quotes the command to worship and serve God alone. Then "the devil left him, and behold, angels came and served him."

Paul explains what this means for us. Through one man, sin entered the world. But "much more did the grace of God and the gift by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many." Christ's obedience undoes Adam's disobedience.

The psalm gives us our Lenten prayer: "Create in me a clean heart, O God." This Lent, choose a verse of Scripture to hold on to when temptation comes. And make a simple plan for prayer, fasting and almsgiving.
